parts: People say an eighteen ninety-one patent settles the toilet paper war: over, not under.
The drawing shows one sheet hanging over the roll.
So we read the patent. All of it.
Seth Wheeler patented it in Albany, New York, on December twenty-second, eighteen ninety-one.
Not one word about how to mount the roll.
It is about perforations: an angled cut, so each sheet tears off cleanly.
Wheeler had patented rolls and wall holders years before this one.
Our reading: to sell the cut, he had to show a sheet. Which way it hung was probably incidental.
In twenty fifteen, a tweet about this patent made the news.
So is over correct? Nobody has shown it.
The full investigation is in the video linked below.
